help_what: NFC terminals are physical devices based on ESP32 installed in stores to accept payments with NFC cards. Each user can have an NFC card linked to their account that contains their unique identifier.
help_purpose: They allow in-person exchange network transactions without needing a computer or phone. The user taps their card on the terminal, enters the amount and their PIN, and the payment is processed automatically.
help_keypad: Terminal with rotary encoder and display. The merchant enters the amount with the encoder and the user confirms with their PIN.
help_touch: Terminal with ILI9341 touchscreen. The merchant enters the amount by tapping the screen.
help_web: The amount is sent from the web or mobile app. The terminal only confirms the card and PIN.
help_community: Dual-card terminal: the user taps their card and the merchant's card. No PIN required, ideal for community markets.
help_ble: NFC reader that connects via Bluetooth to a phone or computer. Useful when no WiFi is available.
help_tab_terminals: List of ESP32 terminals registered on the node. Shows whether they are active and when they were last seen.
help_tab_provision: Process of configuring a new ESP32 terminal. You need to connect it via USB, read its chip ID, and download the compiled firmware.
help_tab_cards: Issue NFC cards for users and change PINs. The card only contains the user's ID, not the private key. If lost, it is deactivated and a new one is issued.
help_tab_tx: History of payments made through NFC terminals.
help_chipid: It is a unique identifier of 12 hexadecimal characters engraved in each ESP32 chip at the factory. It cannot be modified and serves to uniquely identify each physical terminal. It is read with the chip-id-reader.ino sketch or by scanning via USB with Web Serial.
help_token: It is a secret code generated by the server when registering or provisioning a terminal. It is copied into the config.h file of the ESP32 firmware so the terminal can authenticate with the node when connecting for the first time.
help_pairing: The administrator issues an NFC card assigned to a user (User ID) and registers the UID of the physical card. The card is given to the user with an initial PIN that they must change the first time they use it.
help_pin: It is a 4-digit code that protects the NFC card. It is requested from the user in each transaction (except in community mode). If forgotten, the administrator can reset it to a default value.

card_classic_desc: Affordable card with 15 sectors. Each sector has independent Key A (read) and Key B (write). A 16-byte certificate is written, replicated 3 times in the 3 blocks of each sector. Only 1 sector is active at a time. After each payment, the certificate rotates to another random sector. Requires ID document to pay.
card_ntag_desc: Card with AES-128 encryption. On each tap it automatically generates a cryptographic code (MAC) that the server verifies. Anti-cloning: nobody can copy the card without the AES key. More affordable than DESFire EV3.
card_desfire_desc: High security card with full AES-128 challenge-response. The server sends a challenge, the card responds with AES encryption. The most secure option. EV3 = third generation of the DESFire standard.

desc_keypad: ESP32 terminal with rotary encoder and small display. The user turns the encoder to select the amount and confirms with a click. Ideal for markets and fairs where dedicated, rugged hardware is needed.
desc_web: Point of sale in the browser. Ideal for iPhone, computers or any device without an Android app. Can use Bluetooth NFC reader. The client pays by scanning a QR or with NFC card. NOTE: No browser data is needed to register. The terminal is assigned to a user/organization, and the owner approves each browser session from their account (My Points of Sale > POS Web Sessions).
desc_touch: ESP32 terminal with full touchscreen. The seller taps the on-screen buttons to enter the amount. More intuitive than the encoder, ideal for users unfamiliar with dedicated hardware.
desc_community: Dual-card ESP32 terminal for community markets. Reads both the seller's card and the buyer's card in a single transaction. Designed for community barter where both members must be present.
desc_android_pos: Android app (phone or tablet) that works as a point of sale. It pairs with the node via a 6-digit short code. No dedicated hardware needed — uses the seller's phone. Generates charges via QR and NFC. Ideal for sellers who already have an Android phone.
desc_ble_reader: Bluetooth NFC reader (accessory). Not a terminal — it associates with the web or Android POS from the POS app. Not registered here.
